attack_technique: Endpoint Denial of Service: Application Exhaustion Flood
description: Adversaries may target web applications and services with high-volume or prolonged request streams (such as HTTP requests). Tools like GoldenEye exploit HTTP Keep-Alive and Cache-Control features to hold connections open, rapidly exhausting the application's connection pool and preventing legitimate users from accessing the service.

patterns.description: Specific characteristics within the HTTP headers designed to force the server to allocate maximum resources.

features.name: Resource-Intensive Header Manipulation
features.description: Use of specific HTTP headers like 'Connection: Keep-Alive' and 'Cache-Control: no-cache' to force the server to bypass caching mechanisms and keep the TCP/HTTP connection open as long as possible.

features.name: Asymmetric Resource Allocation
features.description: The attack sends relatively small HTTP requests that force the backend server to perform heavy processing or database queries, creating a severe resource imbalance.

patterns.description: Anomalies related to the speed and density of incoming requests.

features.name: High Forward Packet Rate
features.description: A massive surge in packets sent from the client to the server (High Flow Pkts/s and High Fwd Pkts/s) to rapidly consume all available connection slots.

features.name: Low Backward Packet Volume
features.description: The server struggles to respond or its responses are delayed, resulting in a significantly lower rate of backward packets (Low Bwd Pkts/s) and smaller average segment sizes from the server.

patterns.description: Timing behaviors designed to rapidly open connections and persistently hold them.

features.name: Minimal Inter-Arrival Time (Aggressive Initiation)
features.description: The mean time between packets in a flow (Flow IAT Mean) is extremely low during the connection initiation phase, representing an aggressive push to open as many sockets as possible.

features.name: Prolonged Forward IAT (Connection Holding)
features.description: Occasional long pauses between forward packets (High Fwd IAT Max) within an established session, designed to prevent the server from timing out and closing the connection (similar to Slowloris behavior).

patterns.description: Contextual indicators and scenarios that might mimic this specific attack.

features.name: Legitimate Traffic Blending
features.description: GoldenEye traffic utilizes standard web ports (80, 443) and valid HTTP syntax, making it difficult to detect using standard Layer 3/Layer 4 network firewalls without deep packet inspection (WAF).

features.name: Aggressive Crawler Resemblance (False Positive Filtering)
features.description: Misconfigured client applications, aggressive search engine web crawlers, or intensive vulnerability scanners can generate high-frequency HTTP request patterns that mimic GoldenEye.
